native_bindings: src/nucleotide_search.rs retains exactly one restored sentinel-padded BLASTna Vec while consuming the existing OID-ordered preliminary stream; changes OID refill the same capacity, all query lists for that OID borrow the same buffer. Capacity is O(largest visited subject), not an all-database decoded cache.

src/nucleotide_setup.rs expand_nucleotide_subject maps borrowed NCBI4na directly through the original NCBI4NA_TO_BLASTNA table into the padded buffer. It removes the earlier intermediate whole-subject blastna Vec and copy.

Public traceback_subject and traceback_preliminary_subject retain convenience behavior by creating one local expanded owner and delegating to crate-private traceback_preliminary_subject_expanded. Search-wide callers supply the OID-batch owner.

Standard16x16 traceback rows are cloned once into an independent Search-owned matrix, replacing16row allocations/copy per list while allowing statistics to borrow ScoreBlk mutably. Native standard scoring rows are constant for a Search owner; no general custom matrix-update API is claimed.

src/report.rs nucleotide_range(hsp,query,subject_range,subject_origin) reuses original display projection with explicit subject origin and preserves all global coordinates; nucleotide delegates with origin0. examples/native_search.rs converts only each HSP subject interval into a reusable range vector.

No translated core kernel, comparator, statistics formula, loop/tie order, ambiguity mapping or traceback script was changed. No MaybeUninit, unchecked access, bump allocator or all-database permanent cache was introduced.

source_lifetime_evidence.meaning: Fetch one subject for an OID batch before looping query lists
Process query HSP lists against the batch-owned subject
Release subject after the complete OID batch
Aligned sequence assembly iterates alignment segments and reserves row output

focused_validation: cargo test --test nucleotide_initial_search (existing public convenience/report test passed)
Isolated release example built in /tmp/btyper-nucleotide-reuse-target; original final artifact preserved.
